AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate 2 strategies for preparing family members for surrogate decision-making.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: A 2 × 2 factorial, randomized controlled trial testing whether: (1) comprehensive online advance care planning (ACP) is superior to basic ACP, and (2) having patients engage in ACP together with family members is superior to ACP done by patients alone.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: Tertiary care centers in Hershey, Pennsylvania, and Boston, Massachusetts.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: Dyads of patients with advanced, severe illness (mean age 64; 46% female; 72% white) and family members who would be their surrogate decision-makers (mean age 56; 75% female; 75% white).

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTIONS
AbstractText.content: Basic ACP: state-approved online advance directive plus brochure. Making Your Wishes Known (MYWK): Comprehensive ACP decision aid including education and values clarification.

AbstractText.Label: MEASUREMENTS
AbstractText.content: Pre-post changes in family member self-efficacy (100-point scale) and postintervention concordance between patients and family members using clinical vignettes.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: A total 285 dyads enrolled; 267 patients and 267 family members completed measures. Baseline self-efficacy in both MYWK and basic ACP groups was high (90.2 and 90.1, respectively), and increased postintervention to 92.1 for MYWK ( P = .13) and 93.3 for basic ACP ( P = .004), with no between-group difference. Baseline self-efficacy in alone and together groups was also high (90.2 and 90.1, respectively), and increased to 92.6 for alone ( P = .03) and 92.8 for together ( P = .03), with no between-group difference. Overall adjusted concordance was higher in MYWK compared to basic ACP (85.2% vs 79.7%; P = .032), with no between-group difference.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The disconnect between confidence and performance raises questions about how to prepare family members to be surrogate decision-makers.
